title: Personal Weather Impact Cross-Feed Daily Correlation
dataSources: Weather-station readings (`weatherstation:reading`), daily weather-impact rollups (`personalweather:daily`), sleep correlation records (`personalweather:sleep`), step correlation records (`personalweather:steps`), mood correlation records (`personalweather:mood`).
app: Local weather-station readings correlated with personal sleep, steps, mood, and outdoor-activity summaries in Splunk via scripted inputs and daily rollups.
spl:
(index=personal sourcetype=personalweather:sleep) OR (index=personal sourcetype=personalweather:steps)
| bin _time span=1d
| eval feed=case(sourcetype="personalweather:sleep","primary",sourcetype="personalweather:steps","secondary",1=1,"other")
| stats count as events by _time feed
| chart sum(events) over _time by feed
description: Lines up daily volume from personalweather:sleep and personalweather:steps to see whether two personal weather impact feeds move together.
value: When two related exports diverge — one busy, one silent — it usually means a connector broke on only one path.
implementation: Forward both `personalweather:sleep` and `personalweather:steps` into `index=personal` and compare daily counts on one chart.
visualization: Dual-line chart of daily events per sourcetype.
grandmaExplanation: It shows whether your two main personal weather impact data feeds rise and fall together or if one of them quietly stopped keeping up.
